note: Group labels the border layer draws instead of naming a single polity.
why: A capital drawn under a group label is not the same kind of result as a capital drawn under another polity's name, and the capital test used to score them alike.

'Rajput kingdoms' over Jodhpur is a correct but coarse map: Marwar is one of the kingdoms meant. 'Delhi Sultanate' over Jodhpur is a wrong map. Counting both as failures buried the second kind under the first.
So a collective is a pass that is still reported, because it is exactly where the claim layer has work to do. See docs/HANDOFF.md priority 3.

The line: a collective names POLITIES. A label naming a people or a way of life -- 'Bantu peoples', 'Eastern North American hunter-gatherers', 'West African cereal farmers' -- is the source declining to name a state. Where we hold that a state stood there, that stays a failure. Cahokia was a city of some tens of thousands and drawing foragers over it is an error, not a generalisation.
